events.text: At four you are carried before the throne of the Hundred Thousand Mountains for the Rite of the Black Drum. Every child of the blood is shown to the Cult once. The drum is taller than a house. When it sounds, you are supposed not to cry.

effects.log: You do not cry. The Heavenly Demon looks down at you for one breath longer than at the others.
You howl. Half the hall laughs, and an old elder says the loud ones live longest.

events.text: Your mother, the Lady of {hh_house}, teaches you four different bows: one for each house, and none of them the same depth. "The bow tells them what you think of them," she says. "Never let it tell the truth."

effects.log: By six your bows are perfect, and nobody at all can read them.

choices.text: Ask which house she hates most

effects.log: She laughs, and does not answer, and bows to you very slightly: the Lotus bow.

events.text: The Heavenly Demon passes you in a corridor of black stone, with twenty guards behind him. Everyone kneels. He stops, looks at you, and asks your name, though he must know it.

effects.log: You say it clearly. He nods once and walks on. Your nurse has to sit down afterwards.
The guards go white. The Heavenly Demon laughs, a sound nobody in the corridor has heard before, and walks on.

events.text: In the inner halls of {hh_house} the elders hold a council about your future while you play with wooden horses under the table. They forget you are there.

effects.log: You learn that your house has three enemies, two debts and one secret. You keep all six.
An elder lifts the tablecloth, sighs, and carries you out. The council goes on without you, as councils do.

events.text: Behind the paper screens of the Black Lotus House everyone whispers. By six you can tell a lie from the way a shadow moves on the paper. Your mother calls it the house's first art.

effects.log: You learn to read a screen like a book. Nobody can hide a lie from you behind paper.

choices.text: Learn to stand where there is no light

effects.log: You learn to stand where your own shadow does not fall. The house approves.

events.text: The children of the Iron Gate House are taken up onto the Cult's great wall at seven and made to stand one night watch in the wind. You are given a spear twice your height.

effects.log: You stand until dawn and do not sit once. The old gate captain gives you his own cloak.
You count four thousand stars and fall asleep at four thousand and one. The captain lets you.

events.text: The Bone Lantern House keeps the ancestor hall of the Cult. There are eleven thousand lanterns in it, one for each of the blood who ever died, and a child of the house learns to trim their wicks.

effects.log: You trim them for a whole winter. The keeper says the dead like your hands.
You find it, cracked and green with age. The name on it has been scratched out.

events.text: In the Jade Furnace House the children learn to count before they learn to read: pills, silver, debts. You are given an abacus of black jade for your sixth birthday.

effects.log: You count everything in the house, including the cooks. The treasurer adopts you as his favourite.
You find that one pill furnace has lost a jar a month for three years. The house is very interested.

events.text: Pyo Taegang of the Iron Gate House is four years older than you and already as broad as a door. In the practice yard he knocks you flat with a wooden sword, then holds out a hand to help you up.

effects.log: You take it. "Again," he says, and knocks you down again. It is the closest thing to friendship in the yard.
You get up on your own. He looks at you with new interest, the way a soldier looks at a wall.

events.text: Sim Haeryun of the Black Lotus House gives you a candied plum at the New Year banquet and watches you to see if you will eat it. She is nine. She smiles like a grown woman.

effects.log: It is only a plum. She looks a little disappointed, as though she had wanted you to be cleverer.
The dog eats it and is fine. Haeryun laughs and claps. "Good," she says. "Now we can be friends."

events.text: Yeom Sado of the Bone Lantern House, the same age as you and very pale, tells you he has seen your lantern in the hall of the dead. "It is not lit yet," he says. "But it is there."

choices.text: Ask him what his looks like

effects.log: He thinks about it for a long time. "Smaller than yours," he says at last. He does not seem to mind.
He stops. Later you find a single white paper lantern outside your door, which might be an apology.

events.text: Ok Seobin of the Jade Furnace House offers to buy your wooden horse for three sweets now or five sweets next month. She has a little ledger with your name already in it.

effects.log: You eat three sweets. Seobin writes something in her ledger and underlines it.
A month later she pays you five, to the sweet. "You will do well," she says. It sounds like a warning.

events.text: When the consorts walk through the kitchens on the way to the Heavenly Demon's table, the cooks lift you into a rice basket and put the lid on. You learn to breathe very quietly, in the smell of rice.

effects.log: You see four Ladies in four colours of silk, and you memorise every face.
You sleep. Danbi lifts you out afterwards, warm and smelling of rice, and holds you a long time.

events.text: Granny Yun, who has cooked for three Heavenly Demons, teaches you to cut onions without crying. "The trick," she says, "is to keep your ears open and your face shut. That works for everything in these mountains."

effects.log: You learn it. Granny Yun starts to tell you what the maids of the four houses gossip about.
You cry over the onions. Granny Yun pats your head with a floury hand and lets you.

events.text: A maid of the Black Lotus House slaps your mother Danbi for spilling broth on her sleeve. Danbi bows and says nothing. You are seven, and you have a ladle in your hand.

choices.text: Do nothing, and remember her face

effects.log: You remember the maid's face. Years later you will know her name too.
You spill a whole pot on her shoes. The maid screams. Danbi drags you away, and laughs about it all night.

events.text: From the kitchen gallery you see the Heavenly Demon for the first time: a tall figure in black at the end of the great hall, eating alone. The whole hall is silent while he eats. Danbi says that is your father.

effects.log: He looks up. For one moment the Heavenly Demon is looking at the kitchen gallery, at you.
You go back to the onions. A father is a man who eats alone at the end of a hall.

events.text: In the practice yard the heirs of the four houses call you the scullery blood and throw their wooden swords at your feet for you to carry. None of them will spar with you.

effects.log: You carry them. And you watch every one of them fight, every day, from the edge of the yard.

choices.text: Pick one up and swing it

effects.log: You swing it badly. The arms master watches, and says nothing, and the next day there is a fifth wooden sword on the rack.

events.text: Arms Master Tak Yeongsu teaches the blood of the Heavenly Demon their first form of the Divine Palm. He has one eye and a voice like a landslide. "Your father learned this form from me," he says. "He was bad at it."

effects.log: You train until your palms crack. Tak Yeongsu grunts, which from him is a song.
Tak Yeongsu tells you, in detail. It is the most anyone has ever told you about the Heavenly Demon.

events.text: Sim Haeryun finds you on the cliff path at night, as if by accident. "The others will gang up on whoever is strongest," she says. "Let us not be the strongest, together, until it is too late for them."

effects.log: She smiles and pricks her thumb. A pact of the Black Lotus is a strange thing, but it is a pact.

choices.text: Say you will think about it

effects.log: She bows the Lotus bow, the one that says nothing, and is gone.

events.text: Pyo Taegang challenges you to a sparring match in front of the whole yard. He is bigger, older and better. "I do not want to beat you when it matters," he says. "So I will beat you now, and we will both know."

effects.log: He beats you. But he has to work for it, and afterwards he says, quietly, "Not bad." It is a beginning.
You refuse. The yard laughs at you. Taegang does not laugh. He nods as if you had passed something.

events.text: Yeom Sado asks you to hold a lantern for him at midnight in the hall of the dead while he speaks to someone you cannot see. When he is done he says, "The old Heavenly Demon says to tell you: trust the kitchens."

effects.log: He does not know. "The dead do not explain," he says. "That is what makes them restful."
He swears on his own unlit lantern. Something between you is sealed.

events.text: Ok Seobin offers you a jar of the Jade Furnace's best qi-gathering pills, interest-free, "for now". She shows you the ledger where the debt would go, already written in, with a blank where the date should be.

effects.log: The pills are excellent. The blank in the ledger is a thing you will think about for years.
She considers you for a long, cool moment, then crosses out the debt and writes the word partner.

events.text: A kitchen boy is beaten for stealing a pill from the Jade Furnace's store. You stole it, for Danbi's cough. The boy looks at you through the whole beating and does not say your name.

effects.log: You confess. The beating is yours instead. From that day every servant in the mountains is on your side.
You bring him your own rice for a month. He forgives you, and so do the kitchens, a little.

events.text: Danbi sits on the scullery step with you on a cold night and asks you not to fight for the throne. "They will kill you," she says. "I would rather have you cutting onions than in a lantern."

effects.log: You hold her hand and promise nothing, and she knows what that means, and holds on anyway.

choices.text: Promise her a hall of her own

effects.log: You promise her a hall with a garden and nobody to slap her. She laughs and cries at once.

events.text: The elders of {hh_house} begin to teach you the contest: which elder of the Cult owes your house a favour, which one can be frightened, and which one must never, ever be crossed.

effects.log: You learn the list by heart. The elders burn the paper it was written on.
They tell you about Grand Elder Ryu Hwagang, who has kept the empty throne between three Heavenly Demons.

events.text: The Heavenly Demon has every child of the blood brought to the black cliff and told to stand at its edge with their eyes closed until he says to stop. The wind is very strong. He does not say to stop for a long time.

effects.log: You stand until your legs shake. When he finally speaks, he says only your name.
You open your eyes and see that he is standing at the edge too, beside you, with his own closed.

events.text: At the Rite of Counting your name is read before the throne among the blood of the Heavenly Demon, and the four houses turn to look at you. From today, by the oldest law of the Cult, any of the blood may be the next Heavenly Demon.

effects.log: You meet every eye in the hall, one by one. Some of them look away first.
You bow to the empty air above the throne. The elders approve; the houses take note.

events.text: At the Rite of Counting the herald reaches your name and stops. The hall goes silent. Then, because the law is the law, he reads it: the child of Danbi of the kitchens. Someone in the Lotus seats laughs.

effects.log: You walk to the foot of the throne in a kitchen apron. The Heavenly Demon watches you all the way.

choices.text: Look for the one who laughed

effects.log: You find her face and keep it. The Lotus seats go very quiet.

events.text: The council of {hh_house} sits late, arguing over which elder of the Cult to court this year. Halfway through, they stop arguing and look at you.

effects.log: You choose. The council does what you say, which is new, and a little frightening.
You let them argue. A house that argues in front of you trusts you.

events.text: Granny Yun sets a bowl of noodles in front of you at midnight and, while you eat, tells you which of the four houses bought poison from the herb seller this month. "Only for rats," she says. "Big rats."

effects.log: She tells you. You eat the rest of the noodles very slowly.
You thank her. She watches you eat the way she watched you as a baby in the rice basket.

events.text: You send gifts to a house that does not love you and drink their tea, which is very good and very cold. The elders ask after your health with real interest.

effects.log: You ask after every elder's health in turn. By the end of the tea they are almost warm.
You leave half a cup. It is an insult so small that only they will understand it.

events.text: The pact is sealed in the old way of the Cult: a drop of blood in a cup of black tea, drunk half each. Your new ally wipes the cup dry and keeps it.

effects.log: "So that I remember," they say. "And so that you remember that I have it."

choices.text: Keep your half of the leaves

effects.log: You keep the leaves. Both of you understand perfectly.

events.text: The rival heir hears you out with a polite smile. By evening, two houses know every word you said, and one of them has sent you a basket of fruit, which is how the Cult says: we know.

effects.log: It is not poisoned. That is the message.
You send it back untouched. The game goes on.

events.text: You kneel in the Hall of the Heavenly Demon while he reads reports. For an hour he says nothing. Then, without looking up, he asks what you would do about the Cult's border with the orthodox sects.

effects.log: You answer. He looks up, at last, and asks a second question. That has never happened before.
You answer the way he would. "Don't," he says. "I have one of me."

events.text: Arms Master Tak Yeongsu meets you at dawn on the black cliffs and makes you hold the third form of the Divine Palm until the sun is up. "The trial of arms is not won on the day," he says. "It is won now."

effects.log: You hold it. When the sun clears the peaks he nods once. Your arms do not stop shaking until noon.
He spars with you, one-eyed and sixty, and puts you down nine times. The tenth time you stay up.

events.text: The Black Lotus House holds a moon-viewing party in its screened garden, and every guest leaves knowing one secret about another guest. Yours is about the Jade Furnace's treasury.

effects.log: You use it. The Jade Furnace pays you, quietly, to forget it again.
You forget it on purpose. Sim Yeorang of the Lotus notices that you did, and likes you better for it.

events.text: The Iron Gate House parades its guards on the great wall for the Heavenly Demon. One thousand spears, one thousand shouts. The message is for the other houses: the walls are ours.

effects.log: You walk the whole wall with the gate captains. Soldiers remember who walked with them.
There are nine hundred and twelve. You mention it to no one, which the Iron Gate notices.

events.text: The Bone Lantern House announces that a lantern in the hall of the dead has lit itself. It belongs to no one yet. Every house is suddenly very interested in whose it will be.

effects.log: You go and look. The flame leans toward you a little, or perhaps it is the draught.
You stay away. The Bone Lantern House takes that as respect.

events.text: The Jade Furnace House lends the Cult's treasury a fortune for a new war, and lets it be known who else owes it money. Your name is not on the list, yet.

effects.log: You borrow nothing. Ok Damhui of the Furnace calls you the only free child of the blood.
You borrow and buy friends with it. Now your name is on the list.

events.text: Sim Haeryun sends you a letter folded into a paper lotus. Inside is one line: the name of an elder who has promised his vote to two heirs at once.

effects.log: You expose him at council. He loses his seat; two houses lose their vote; Haeryun smiles.
You keep it. A secret given by the Lotus is a debt, and debts can be useful.

events.text: Pyo Taegang wins a border skirmish against the orthodox sects and rides back into the mountains with the enemy's banner over his saddle. The Cult cheers him all the way up the black steps.

effects.log: You cheer as loud as anyone. Taegang sees you in the crowd and raises the banner to you.
You ask, quietly. Forty. He looks at you differently after that, as if you were the only one who asked.

events.text: Yeom Sado has stopped sleeping. The Bone Lantern's healers say he spends his nights in the hall of the dead, asking eleven thousand lanterns who will win.

effects.log: You sit with him until dawn. The lanterns say nothing. Sado says that is an answer too.
You let him. A rival who will not sleep is a rival who will not last.

events.text: Ok Seobin buys the debts of half the Cult's middle elders in a single season. At council they vote the way she coughs. Every heir is suddenly polite to her.

choices.text: Buy one debt back from under her

effects.log: You buy one back. Seobin writes your name in her ledger with a little star beside it.
You are polite. So is she. The ledger stays closed between you, for now.

events.text: The Heavenly Demon calls you to walk with him on the black cliffs. He talks about the weather, the harvest of the valley farms and an old sword he lost when he was young. He never mentions the throne.

effects.log: He tells you the whole story. It is the longest anyone has heard him speak in twenty years.
He stops walking. "Ask me again when you have earned the question," he says, and walks on.

events.text: At the great feast the Heavenly Demon raises his cup to every child of the blood in turn. He forgets you. Or he does not forget you, which is worse. The houses watch your face.

choices.text: Raise your own cup to him

effects.log: You raise your cup to the throne, alone, in the silence. Some elders hide a smile.
You keep eating as if nothing happened. The houses decide you are harder to hurt than they thought.

events.text: Danbi has grown thin, and the four houses' maids still order her about. Granny Yun says the Heavenly Demon asked after her, once, last winter, and nobody told her.

effects.log: You tell her. She sits down on a sack of rice and laughs, and then does not laugh.

choices.text: Ask the Heavenly Demon for her

effects.log: You ask, at audience, before the houses. The hall gasps. The Heavenly Demon says he will think about it.

events.text: The killer the guards caught at your door is a thin man with no tongue and a needle sewn into his sleeve. Somebody's house paid him. The guards want to know what to do with him.

effects.log: You drag him before the throne and name the house that hired him. The hall goes very quiet.

choices.text: Send him back to his house, alive

effects.log: You send him back with a cup of tea. The house that hired him understands you are not afraid, and is afraid.

events.text: The cook's boy who woke you sits shaking in the kitchen with Granny Yun's arm around him. "He was on the roof for an hour," the boy says. "I heard him breathing."

choices.text: Give the boy your jade pendant

effects.log: You give him your jade pendant. The kitchens will remember it for a hundred years.

choices.text: Ask the boy what the man smelled of

effects.log: Incense from the hall of the dead, the boy says. You file that away carefully.

events.text: You lie for a week with a black wound in your shoulder while the Cult's physicians argue about the poison. Every house sends flowers. One of the bouquets is from the house that tried to kill you.

choices.text: Thank every house for the flowers

effects.log: You thank every one, in your own hand. One house will lie awake over your letter.
You find out. You do nothing, yet. A wound is a debt too.

events.text: Arms Master Tak Yeongsu comes to your sickbed and looks at the scar. "A needle, from above," he says. "An old way. The Heavenly Demon had one of those too, on the other shoulder."

choices.text: Ask who gave it to him

effects.log: He tells you, and you understand the Cult a little better. The one who gave it is a lantern now.

choices.text: Ask him to teach you to hear a roof

effects.log: He teaches you. You will not sleep soundly again, and you will not be surprised again.

events.text: Your ally of the pact stands up at council and repeats, word for word, a plan you told them in secret. Their house has turned, and they have turned with it. They do not meet your eyes.

effects.log: You deny everything, calmly. Half the council believes you. The other half was never going to.

choices.text: Admit it, and say who told them

effects.log: You admit it and look at your old ally. The council sees two heirs who cannot be trusted, and one who can.

events.text: The cup from your blood pact is returned to you, washed clean, on a lacquered tray. It is the oldest message in the Hundred Thousand Mountains.

effects.log: You smash it on the black stone. Everyone in the courtyard hears.
You put it on your shelf where every visitor will see it. Let them wonder.

events.text: The black drums beat for nine days. On the tenth Grand Elder Ryu Hwagang, who has kept the empty throne between three Heavenly Demons, sets a stool beside it and sits. "Three trials," he says. "Arms. The houses. The elders. Begin."

effects.log: You bow to him, not to the throne. The old man's eyebrows rise by a hair.
You look at the throne. It is only a chair of black stone. Everyone in the hall is looking at it too.

events.text: The black drums beat for nine days. In the kitchens nobody sleeps. On the tenth morning Granny Yun brings you rice and says, "Every cook in these mountains is listening for you. Go and be counted."

effects.log: You go to the trials in a kitchen apron. The heirs laugh. Grand Elder Ryu Hwagang does not.
The kitchens have sewn you a robe of black silk out of a hundred scraps. You wear it.

events.text: On the black stone before the empty throne you face the strongest heir still standing. When it is over you are the one on your feet, and the Cult has seen it.

effects.log: You help them up in front of the whole hall. It costs you nothing and buys you a great deal.

choices.text: Turn your back and walk away

effects.log: You walk away without a word. The Cult understands that kind of victory too.

events.text: You lie on the black stone with the hall spinning above you. The strongest of the heirs looks down at you, breathing hard. Grand Elder Ryu Hwagang writes something with a very small brush.

effects.log: You get up. The trial is lost, but the Cult saw you get up.
You lie there and look at the ceiling, which is painted with stars. You have never noticed.

events.text: The four houses cast their lacquered tokens into the bronze bowl, black, red, white and green. When Grand Elder Ryu Hwagang tips the bowl out, the colours have come your way.

effects.log: You thank each house by name. Even the one that voted against you.

choices.text: Thank the one who changed their vote

effects.log: You catch one elder's eye and nod. They will never be able to deny it now.

events.text: The four houses cast their tokens into the bronze bowl. Too few are yours. A Jade Furnace elder will not look at you; a Black Lotus elder looks at you far too much.

effects.log: You remember every token. There will be other bowls.
You shrug. The trial of the houses was always theirs to give.

events.text: The elders of the Cult sit in a ring and weigh what the Heavenly Demon thought of each of the blood. One by one they set a white stone before you.

effects.log: You bow to every elder. The oldest of them says, "He spoke of you." That is all.
Grand Elder Ryu Hwagang tells you. You will keep it all your life.

events.text: The elders of the Cult sit in a ring and set their white stones before another heir. Grand Elder Ryu Hwagang sets his own before no one at all, and looks at you for a long time.

effects.log: "Because the throne is not won by stones," he says. You think about that for years.
You leave the ring. Behind you an elder sighs, and you cannot tell what it means.

events.text: You sit the throne of the Hundred Thousand Mountains. It is cold, and much harder than it looks. Below you the Cult bows its ten thousand heads, and the four houses bow lowest of all.

effects.log: You speak. The Cult listens to a new voice for the first time in thirty years.
You say nothing at all. The silence is exactly the silence they remember.

events.text: You sit the throne of the Hundred Thousand Mountains in a robe the kitchens sewed from a hundred scraps. Below you the four houses bow, and behind them, at the back of the hall, every cook in the mountains.

effects.log: You bow, from the throne, to the back of the hall. No Heavenly Demon has ever done it.
Danbi comes up the black steps in a new robe, shaking. You give her the seat at your right hand.

events.text: You kneel first, before any of the blood, and the new Heavenly Demon lifts you up in front of the whole Cult. "The first to kneel," they say, "sits at my right hand." It is a chair, and it is close to the throne.

effects.log: You take the chair. A Cult Elder of the blood is a dangerous friend, and you both know it.

choices.text: Ask for a hall in the mountains instead

effects.log: You ask for a quiet hall far from the black steps. It is granted, with relief.

events.text: You go down the mountain by the goat path with one bag and your arts. Behind you the black drums begin again, for someone else. Ahead of you is the whole murim, which has never heard your name.

effects.log: You walk until the peaks are a line of teeth on the horizon.
You look back once, at the Hundred Thousand Mountains. Then you do not look back again.

events.text: A child of the blood is born in the inner halls of the Cult, your own, and the four houses send gifts before the midwife has washed her hands. You understand now why the old Heavenly Demon ate alone.

effects.log: You eat with the whole household at one table, the first Heavenly Demon to do it in memory.
You eat alone at the end of the hall. It is very quiet. It is also very clear.

events.text: Grand Elder Ryu Hwagang dies at ninety-one, in his chair beside the throne, while you hear a petition. You finish hearing it before you call the physicians, as he would have wanted.

effects.log: You light his lantern in the hall of the dead with your own hands.

choices.text: Leave his stool beside the throne

effects.log: You leave the stool where it is. Nobody sits on it again in your reign.

events.text: From your chair at the new Heavenly Demon's right hand you watch them make the mistakes you would have made. You say so, once, in private. They listen, which surprises you both.

effects.log: You keep advising, quietly. A throne has two chairs, it turns out.

choices.text: Stop, before it is too much

effects.log: You stop. A Cult Elder who advises too well becomes a rival again.

events.text: In a teahouse far from the mountains a stranger at the next table recognises the way you hold your cup: the way of the inner halls of the Cult. He pays for your tea and leaves without a word.

effects.log: He is a runaway of the Cult too, a cook. You talk all night.
You let him go. Some debts should be left on the table.

events.text: Passing the foothills of the Hundred Thousand Mountains you stop dead. You know, without knowing how, how cold the black throne at the top of them is, and how hard.

effects.log: You go on. The mountains watch you go. Your soul has sat up there before.
You turn back. Some chairs should only be sat in once.

events.text: The smell of rice steaming in a big basket stops you in a market street. For a moment you are very small, and someone is lifting a lid, and a woman is laughing.

effects.log: You buy a bowl and eat it standing in the street. It tastes like a past life.
You walk on, and the smell follows you a while.

events.text: On a goat path in the hills you find your feet know the way down, every loose stone of it, in the dark. You have never been here before, in this life.

effects.log: Your feet take you down safely. Your soul fled this way once, and lived.
You sit on a rock until dawn, and the feeling fades.

events.text: In a temple a painted ring of white stones on a black floor makes your heart race. You kneel at the edge of it without meaning to, as if waiting to be weighed.

effects.log: Nothing happens. You laugh at yourself. Your soul does not laugh.
You leave quickly. Some trials are lost in a past life and stay lost.

events.text: An old Cult Elder on the road bows to you, deeply, and then stops, confused. "Forgive me," he says. "For a moment I thought you were someone who once knelt first."

effects.log: You bow back. Something in you is very old, and pleased.
He tells you of a child of the blood who knelt first and lived long. You know the ending already.

events.text: The consort of the Black Lotus House arrives behind a screen of black lacquer and speaks to you through it on the wedding night, so that you hear a voice before you see a face. "The house will want things," says the voice. "I will tell you which ones to give."

effects.log: The Hall of the Heavenly Demon is a little warmer tonight.
You ask. The answer is long, honest, and very useful.

events.text: The consort of the Iron Gate House arrives on horseback, not in the palanquin, with a spear across the saddle. "The house sent me to guard the throne," says the consort. "I would rather guard you. We will see."

effects.log: The Hall of the Heavenly Demon is a little warmer tonight.
You ask. The answer is long, honest, and very useful.

events.text: The consort of the Bone Lantern House brings one lantern up the black steps, unlit, and sets it beside your bed. "For the day the hall of the dead needs yours," says the consort. "I hope I never light it."

effects.log: The Hall of the Heavenly Demon is a little warmer tonight.
You ask. The answer is long, honest, and very useful.

events.text: The consort of the Jade Furnace House brings a dowry of pills and a ledger. On the first page of the ledger is your name, and beside it, in a careful hand: no debt.

effects.log: The Hall of the Heavenly Demon is a little warmer tonight.
You ask. The answer is long, honest, and very useful.

events.text: Two of your children of different houses fight in the practice yard, and both consorts come to you in the same hour, each with a long account of whose fault it was. Both accounts are perfect. Neither is true.

effects.log: You punish both. Both houses are furious, equally, which is a kind of peace.

choices.text: Send both consorts to the yard to watch

effects.log: They watch their children make up without them. Neither consort forgives you, and both forgive the children.

events.text: At the New Year feast each consort house seats its own child of your blood nearer to the throne than the others, and the stewards have to move the tables four times before the soup.

effects.log: You seat them by age. Every house is offended, and every child is relieved.
You have every table in the hall made round. The carpenters work all night.

events.text: A consort house sends you a gift of a sword for one of your children and nothing for the others. It is a very good sword. That is the problem.

effects.log: You give it to a child of another house. The giver learns not to do that again.

choices.text: Hang it on the wall of the hall

effects.log: You hang it on the wall: a sword for whoever earns it. Every child of yours trains harder.

events.text: A house you passed over sends its consort to you with tea and no smile, and the next night a servant of your named heir is found with a purse of that house's silver. The heir is unharmed. The message is not.

choices.text: Shame the house before the throne

effects.log: You shame the house before the whole Cult. It bows lower than it ever has, and hates you more.
You speak to the consort alone, all night. By morning the house has let it go, for now.

events.text: Your named heir comes to you with a note found in their rice: three characters in a house's private cipher. Not a threat. A promise to wait.

effects.log: You double the guard. The house sees it and, for a while, waits.

choices.text: Teach the heir to read the cipher

effects.log: You teach them. Next time, the heir will read it first.

events.text: You set your hand on your heir's head before the whole Cult. The house of the heir weeps for joy; the others bow, all at the same depth, which in these mountains is a warning.

effects.log: You meet each house's eyes in turn. One by one they look away.
You embrace your heir in front of the Cult, which has not seen a Heavenly Demon do that before.
